items.readme_text:
T3 Code

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

Download · iOS · Android · Web · Docs · Discord

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any [ACP](./docs/user/providers-acp.md) agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it. ## What you get - **Your subscriptions.** T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to. - **Every agent in one place.** Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex. - **Desktop, web, and phone.** One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android. - **Remote ready.** Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or [T3 Connect](./docs/user/remote-access.md). - **Git built in.** Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button. - **Fast.** Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug. - **Open.** MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it. ## Install ### Desktop app [Download T3 Code](https://t3.codes/download) for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager: | Platform | Command | | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS | `brew install --cask t3-code` | | Windows | `winget install T3Tools.T3Code` or `scoop install extras/t3code` | | Arch Linux | `yay -S t3code-bin` | | Nix | `nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code` | | Debian, Ubuntu | `.deb` from [Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases) | ### Command line This installs the `t3` command. Run `t3` to start the server and open the web app. ```bash curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex ``` To try it once without an install, run `npx t3@latest`. ### Phone Get the app from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code). Then follow [remote access](./docs/user/remote-access.md) to connect it to your computer. ### Sign in to an agent T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`, or install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`. [Provider setup](./docs/user/install.md#providers) has the steps for each agent. [Install T3 Code](./docs/user/install.md) covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS. ## "Wait, what are you selling me?" Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar. We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want. ## Documentation - [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md) - [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md) - [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md) - [Source control](./docs/user/source-control.md) - [Connect outside agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md) - [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md) [All docs](./docs/README.md) has the full list. ## Contributing We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first. - Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before you report a bug or open a pull request. - Put feature requests in [Ideas](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas). - Build from source with the [development runbook](./docs/operations/00_development.md#first-checkout). The [architecture overview](./docs/internals/01_architecture.md) explains how it works. - Get help in [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

items.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 82 skills, 15 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerability classes, plus enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices.
items.readme_text:
![claude-bughunter banner](assets/banner-v2.svg) # claude-bughunter > A self-contained Claude skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work · **83 skills** · 15 slash commands · **681 disclosed-report patterns** (433 now individually cited & auditable) across 24 core vulnerability classes · enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices · engagement-folder scaffolding · Burp MCP integration · battle-tested across authorized red-team and bug-hunting engagements, plus public training platforms (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101, testphp.vulnweb.com). Built by **[Sachin Sharma](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sachinsharma8080/)** — Bug Hunting & GenAI Security Research.

SPONSORED BY

      

--- ## What is this? `claude-bughunter` is a drop-in skill bundle for the [Claude Code skills system](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills). Install once and Claude Code stops being a chatbot and starts behaving like a senior bug-hunting researcher or red-team operator: it knows the techniques, the chain templates, the VRT mappings, the platform CVE chains, and the hygiene — and it stays in scope. Four layers stack: - **Think** — `bb-methodology` + `redteam-mindset`: the 5-phase non-linear workflow, critical-thinking framework, and red-team operator discipline. - **Hunt webapps** — 58 `hunt-*` skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates. - **Hit the perimeter** — enterprise platform chains (M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, SSL-VPN appliances, SharePoint, cloud IAM): current 2024–2026 CVE chains + post-credential escalation. - **Ship it** — `triage-validation` + reporting + `evidence-hygiene`: the 7-Question Gate, VRT-aware severity, OOS rebuttals, PII redaction, and red-team deliverables. All triggered automatically by topic — describe what you're testing in plain English and the relevant skill loads. No invocation by name. --- ## Quickstart **Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).** From inside Claude Code: ```text /plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter /plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls ``` All 83 skills + 15 commands load namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` and update when you bump the plugin version — no files copied into `~/.claude/`. **A HackerOne account is optional.** The install asks for a HackerOne API username and token. They only let the HackerOne MCP read your private programs and your own reports; leave both blank if you don't need that. Every skill, command and the MCP's public tools (duplicate search, program scope) work without them. **Option B — copy install (no plugin system / pin to a clone):** ```bash git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git cd Claude-BugHunter ``` ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 ``` Both copy the skills + commands into `~/.claude/` (macOS/Linux) or `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows) and wire the `hunt` engagement scaffolder. **What each install path gives you:** | Path | 83 skills + 15 slash commands | `cbh` CLI | `hunt` scaffolder | |---|---|---|---| | **A — plugin** | ✅ namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` | ➕ separate `pipx install` | ❌ clone-only | | **B — copy install** | ✅ copied into `~/.claude/` | ✅ from the clone | ✅ from the clone | The plugin is the fastest path to the skills + slash commands. The terminal-native `cbh` runner installs standalone — `pipx install git+https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter` — so plugin users can add it without a full clone (see [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md)). The `hunt` engagement scaffolder ships with the clone (Option B). That's it. Open Claude Code and describe what you're testing in plain English — the right skill loads automatically, no invocation by name: ```text > Testing acme.com — an in-scope HackerOne target. Run recon and rank the surface. ⟳ loading skills: web2-recon, offensive-osint, bb-methodology … → subdomain enum (subfinder + crt.sh) … 47 hosts → live hosts (httpx) … 12 · tech fingerprint … 6 distinct stacks → ranked surface: api.acme.com (GraphQL, introspection ON) ← start here auth.acme.com (OAuth, SSO) ← hunt-oauth Next: want me to probe the GraphQL introspection + OAuth redirect_uri? ``` → Full [Installation guide](INSTALL.md) · [Usage guide](USAGE.md) · [searchable skill catalog](docs/skills.md). > The block above is an illustrative transcript. To record a real demo of your own session: `asciinema rec demo.cast` → upload to [asciinema.org](https://asciinema.org) and drop the badge here. --- ## Runs on multiple agent harnesses ![One install, agent harnesses — Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Hermes Agent, Google AntiGravity](assets/harness-routing.svg) The skills are plain [Agent Skills](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills) — the same `SKILL.md` format that **Claude Code · OpenCode · OpenAI Codex CLI · Hermes Agent · Google AntiGravity** all load. One command installs them everywhere: ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh --all --burp-mcp # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 -All -BurpMcp ``` | Harness | Target Skill Directory | Flag | |---|---|---| | **Claude Code** (baseline) | `~/.claude/skills/` | *(default)* | | **OpenCode** | reads `~/.claude/skills/` & `~/.agents/skills/` | *(default)* / `--agents` | | **OpenAI Codex CLI** | `~/.agents/skills/` | `--agents` | | **Hermes Agent** | `~/.hermes/skills/` | `--hermes` | | **Google AntiGravity** | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | `--antigravity` | `--all` (`-All`) detects installed harnesses and copies skills to each harness's path (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.hermes/skills`, `~/.gemini/config/skills`); `--burp-mcp` (`-BurpMcp`) wires the Burp MCP server into each. The full *knowledge* layer ports to all five — the slash commands and `/hunt` engine stay Claude-Code-only by design. → [Multi-harness guide](docs/multi-harness.md) --- ## Star History Chart is self-hosted — regenerate with `python3 scripts/gen_star_history.py` (needs `gh auth login`). Refreshes automatically each day via `.github/workflows/star-history.yml`. --- ## Scope — what this bundle is for, and what it isn't This bundle covers the **external attack surface** — anything reachable from the internet without first compromising an internal endpoint. ### In scope - **Bug bounty hunting** — web apps, APIs, SaaS, GraphQL, OAuth, JWT, file upload, IDOR, SSRF, RCE chains - **Web application pentesting** — full hunt-* coverage of OWASP-mapped bug classes + discipline rules - **External red-team engagements** — initial-access against internet-facing enterprise estate: M365 / Entra ID, Okta-as-IdP, SharePoint on-prem (ToolShell + legacy SOAP), VMware vCenter / Workspace ONE, SSL VPN appliances (Cisco / Fortinet / Citrix / Palo Alto / Pulse / SonicWall / F5), Android APK red-team, supply-chain recon - **Cloud misconfig + post-credential escalation** — public S3, IMDS chains, STS AssumeRole, cross-account confused-deputy - **Recon + OSINT** — subdomain enum, identity-fabric mapping, certificate transparency, JS analysis, secret scanning - **Reporting** — H1, Bugcrowd (VRT-aware), Intigriti, Immunefi, plus client-facing red-team deliverable format ### Out of scope (deliberate — not gaps, design decisions) - **Internal Active Directory attacks** — BloodHound, Kerberoasting, ASREProast, DCSync, Pass-the-Hash, AD CS abuse, ntlmrelayx, Responder, PetitPotam, etc. Different operational risk profile; needs different tooling and judgment. **Future bundle, not this one.** - **C2 frameworks** — Cobalt Strike, Sliver, Mythic, Havoc, BRC4 tradecraft. Out of scope for external-only engagement model. - **Post-exploit / persistence / lateral** — Mimikatz/comsvcs LSASS dumping, golden/silver tickets, named-pipe impersonation, persistence (registry, scheduled tasks, WMI events, COM hijacking), token theft. These start after the perimeter has already broken — different bundle territory. - **Evasion** — AMSI bypass, ETW patching, AV/EDR bypass. Tied to C2 tradecraft above. - **iOS pentesting / hardware / RF / ICS** — out of scope by design. - **Binary exploitation / kernel pwn / browser internals** — different skill universe. If you're running an internal red team that includes domain-takeover chains via Kerberos or lateral movement, **this bundle won't help you in those phases** — and we'd rather say that up front than have you find out mid-engagement. The external surface handoff to internal-RT tooling (Impacket, NetExec, CrackMapExec, Rubeus, Certify, BloodHound) is intentionally outside our scope. **Coverage for internal AD and post-exploit may come in a future update.** --- ## What's inside **83 skills**, auto-loaded by topic — no invocation by name. Coverage across the external attack surface: | Category | # | Examples | |---|---|---| | Hunt — web app vuln classes | 58 | XSS, SQLi, SSRF, IDOR, LFI, SSTI, XXE, CSRF, CORS, open-redirect, SharePoint, ASP.NET/NTLM | | Enterprise platform attack ★ | 10 | M365/Entra, Okta, cloud-IAM-deep, vCenter, enterprise VPN, APK/iOS red-team pipelines, supply-chain recon | | Reporting & validation | 6 | triage-validation, evidence-hygiene, report-writing, bugcrowd-reporting | | Recon & OSINT | 5 | web2-recon, offensive-osint, osint-methodology, recon-scope-triage | | Methodology & mindset | 4 | bb-methodology, bug-bounty, redteam-mindset, bb-local-toolkit | Full searchable catalog → **[docs/skills.md](docs/skills.md)**. Also ships **15 slash commands** (`/hunt`, `/recon`, `/report`, …) and a deterministic **engagement engine** (`engine/`) that maps a target's attack surface and routes each finding to the skill that handles it. --- ## How it works A 6-phase, non-linear workflow — **recon → map & rank → hunt → validate → report** — with scope enforced in code and a **7-Question Gate** before anything is submitted. Two ways to drive it: - **Plain English** — describe what you're testing and the relevant skill loads automatically. - **`/hunt` scaffold + `cbh` CLI** — engagement-folder structure, state, and orchestration. → [Usage guide & worked example](USAGE.md) · [6-phase architecture & skill-to-phase map](docs/architecture.md) · [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md) --- ## Authorization These skills are intended for assets you **own** or have **written authorization to assess** (bug-bounty in-scope assets, pentest engagement letters, CTF challenges, your own infrastructure). The skills include validation gates that auto-trigger when you point Claude at unverified third-party targets — `triage-validation`'s 7-Question Gate explicitly asks whether the asset is in scope (Q3) and on the program's accepted-impact list (Q2). The `bugcrowd-reporting` skill includes researcher-side hygiene (Bugcrowdninja alias, account-state restoration, friendly-tester posture) that signals legitimate authorized testing to the target's fraud team. The bundle explicitly **excludes**: weaponizing 0-days against unauthorized targets, post-exploitation tooling, malware development, mass-targeting infrastructure. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) for the full posture. > **Heads-up — Anthropic runtime cyber safeguards.** Anthropic's models apply real-time safeguards that **block "vulnerability exploitation or offensive security tooling development" by default** — so even *authorized, in-scope* work can hit a refusal that isn't this bundle's doing. If you do authorized offensive security (pentest / bug bounty / red team), enroll in Anthropic's **free, application-based [Cyber Verification Program (CVP)](https://claude.com/form/cyber-use-case)** to get safeguards adjusted for legitimate dual-use work. (Mass data exfiltration and ransomware development stay prohibited and are *not* adjustable.) Details: [Anthropic — real-time cyber safeguards](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604842-real-time-cyber-safeguards-on-claude). ### Why your model switched mid-session Separate from refusals, and easy to miss. On **Opus 5**, a narrow set of higher-risk cyber requests — Anthropic names *exploit generation*, *binary-based vulnerability scanning* and *penetration testing* — **fall back to Opus 4.8** rather than being refused. You get a notice and the response is labelled with the model that answered, but in a long agentic run that is easy to scroll past, so it can look like Opus 5 quietly got worse. See [why Claude switched models](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16049681-why-claude-switched-models-in-your-conversation-with-opus-5). What to do depends on what you are actually doing: | Situation | What helps | |---|---| | **Auditing your own code** — reviewing a repo you own for defects | Say so. "Defensive review of my own repo", "check this against the OWASP Top 10", "secure refactor to remediate" describe the work accurately and read as remediation. This is not a workaround; the work genuinely is defensive. | | **Authorized offensive work** — live engagement, PoC for a bounty submission | This is what the bundle is for, and the supported route is [CVP](https://claude.com/form/cyber-use-case). Do not reword an offensive engagement to look defensive to get past a classifier — enroll instead. | | **You just want the switching off** | Settings → Capabilities disables automatic model switching. | `/hunt` states the engagement frame (authorized, scope-bounded, remediable finding) on its first turn for exactly this reason — engagement context belongs in the session explicitly, not implied. --- ## Documentation | Doc | Contents | |---|---| | [`README.md`](README.md) | This file — overview, quickstart, scope, skill summary | | [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md) | Full setup with Burp MCP integration and optional skill regenerator | | [`USAGE.md`](USAGE.md) | Workflow walkthrough · decision tree · worked engagement example | | [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | 6-phase architecture · skill-to-phase mapping · engagement composition | | [`docs/cbh-cli.md`](docs/cbh-cli.md) | `cbh` CLI — native runner orchestrating recon + classify + triage + report | | [`docs/cve-coverage.md`](docs/cve-coverage.md) | CISA KEV coverage snapshot — refreshed weekly via the workflow template at `docs/automation/cve-refresh.yml.template` | | [`docs/credits.md`](docs/credits.md) | Full attribution: 43 original skills + 8 vendored from upstream | | [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) | PR guidelines · skill quality standards · scope | | [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) | Authorized-use posture · responsible disclosure · what's excluded | | [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) | MIT | | [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) | Upstream-skills attribution · no-redistribution note | | [`LICENSE-CONTENT`](LICENSE-CONTENT) | CC BY 4.0 (skill methodology, wordlists, docs) | --- ## Why this exists Most bug-hunting Claude setups are either too generic (one big "security" prompt) or too fragmented (you bookmark 30 disclosed reports and re-read them every engagement). Neither scales past the second target. This bundle was built and validated through authorized engagements that exposed different capability gaps: **Bug-bounty engagement** — surfaced four gaps a starter 3-skill stack could not close: 1. **No hypothesis discipline** — drafts written before validation → wasted hours, hurt validity ratio 2. **No per-program reporting tactics** — VRT defaults auto-downgraded P3-worthy findings to P4 3. **No engagement coordination** — findings, evidence, and submission IDs scattered across folders 4. **No evidence hygiene** — screenshots leaked cookies and victim PII **External red-team engagement** — exposed five additional gaps that bug-bounty defaults made worse: 1. **Conservative defaults retracted real findings** — WAPT mindset stopped tests early on defended targets where red-team continuation would have surfaced bypass chains → `redteam-mindset` 2. **No mid-engagement situational awareness** — client SOC patched confirmed SQLi within 30 min; external attacker locked 14 accounts during a live test session — both invisible without explicit detection methodology → `mid-engagement-ir-detection` 3. **No enterprise-platform attack chains** — M365 + Entra ID, on-prem SharePoint, Cisco SSL VPN, vCenter, and 7 Android APKs all needed current 2024-2026 CVE knowledge and platform-specific tradecraft → `m365-entra-attack`, `okta-attack`, `hunt-sharepoint`, `hunt-aspnet`, `hunt-ntlm-info`, `vmware-vcenter-attack`, `enterprise-vpn-attack`, `apk-redteam-pipeline` 4. **No client-facing deliverable format** — bug-bounty report templates don't fit enterprise red-team where output is a 50KB+ MD + DOCX with embedded screenshots → `redteam-report-template` 5. **No post-credential escalation model** — when recon yielded credentials (AWS keys, JWTs, GCP JSON), it was unclear what they granted or how to escalate → `cloud-iam-deep` The per-class `hunt-*` skills address gap-zero (*"what should I look for in webapps"*) — the original 24 codifying patterns from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports, with 20+ framework/surface skills added by the community v3 expansion — Claude knows the actual chain templates real triagers paid for, not abstract OWASP Top 10. The enterprise-platform and red-team-tradecraft layers address what bug-bounty alone cannot: external red-team engagements against monitored enterprise targets. --- ## Roadmap - [x] HackerOne MCP integration — [`mcp/hackerone/`](mcp/hackerone/README.md): disclosed-report duplicate search, program stats and scope; optional logged-in mode for private programs and your own reports - [ ] Per-engagement memory layer — pattern recall across targets - [x] Industry-specific hunt skills — `hunt-fintech-graphql` shipped; `hunt-healthcare-fhir`, `hunt-gov-compliance` still open - [ ] Program-rules-parser skill — auto-generate structured `scope.md` from program text - [ ] Refresh `hunt-*` skills with newer disclosed reports (re-run `public-skills-builder`) - [ ] Additional enterprise-platform skills — `citrix-netscaler-deep`, `f5-bigip-attack`, `ad-cs-attack` (AD Certificate Services) - [ ] Refresh enterprise-VPN CVE matrix quarterly to track 2026 advisories - [ ] Update architecture SVG to include the 7-skill enterprise-platform layer --- ## Sponsors

**[ApiSmart](https://www.apismart.ai/)** unifies leading LLM, image, and video models through one OpenAI-compatible API. Use one key to switch models, simplify billing, and improve reliability with automatic failover.

**[ThreatWatch360](https://threatwatch360.com)** is an AI-powered offensive-security platform: continuous Attack Surface Management, AI-assisted penetration testing, brand protection, dark-web monitoring, and Cyber Threat Intelligence in one platform. Validated findings with proof-of-concept and business-impact prioritization — signal over alert fatigue. --- ## About Operational tradecraft accumulated across bug-bounty engagements and authorized pentests, codified into Claude skills. Platform-agnostic — slot into any engagement workflow you already use, or none. **Author:** [ElementalSoul](https://github.com/elementalsouls) · GenAI Security Research **Sister project:** [Claude-OSINT](https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-OSINT) — paired skills for the recon phase that this bundle picks up after. Its two recon skills (`offensive-osint`, `osint-methodology`) are **canonically maintained here** and re-exported there, so the two are byte-identical. **Installing both is safe:** each bundle's installer (`install.sh` on macOS/Linux, `install.ps1` on Windows) records a manifest, the script skips re-copying an identical skill, and `--uninstall` keeps any skill the other bundle still owns — uninstalling one never breaks the other. **Vendored foundation:** [shuvonsec/claude-bug-bounty](https://github.com/shuvonsec/claude-bug-bounty) — methodology, validation, reporting, payload library (8 of 83 skills + 15 slash commands) **Generator tool used (not vendored):** [shuvonsec/public-skills-builder](https://github.com/shuvonsec/public-skills-builder) — used to scaffold per-class skills from H1 disclosed reports **Inspirations:** - [archangel / douglasday](https://hackerone.com/) — top-10 H1 hunter; per-class skill pattern - [Trail of Bits — `trailofbits/skills`](https://github.com/trailofbits/skills) — skill-authoring discipline - [SecSkills — `trilwu/secskills`](https://github.com/trilwu/secskills) — subagent pattern **Tool inventory:** - [PortSwigger Burp Suite + MCP Server extension](https://portswigger.net/burp) - [ProjectDiscovery](https://github.com/projectdiscovery) — subfinder · dnsx · httpx · katana · nuclei - [SecLists](https://github.com/danielmiessler/SecLists) · [Assetnote Wordlists](https://wordlists.assetnote.io/) ## License This project is dual-licensed: - **Code** (Python helpers, shell scripts) — [MIT](LICENSE). - **Content** (skill methodology, wordlists, regex catalogs, severity rubrics, docs) — [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](LICENSE-CONTENT) (CC BY 4.0). To be precise about the boundary: **`*.py`, `*.sh`, and other source files are MIT; `*.md` documentation, wordlists, regex catalogs, and rubrics are CC BY 4.0.** Reuse the content freely — including commercially — as long as you credit **Sachin Sharma / Claude-BugHunter** and link back to this repository. See [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) for upstream-skills attribution. --- > *"Give Claude the right skill and it stops being a chatbot. It becomes an operator."*

Orca

中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Português · Türkçe · Русский

Bots inside your agent IDE.

Open source. Bring your own everything: your Claude Code or Codex, your local or remote machines, your tools. Ask from Slack or your phone. When it needs you, it's one tab away.

Download Orca  ·  Explore bots →

## Features
### Orca Bots Ask a bot in Slack, Linear, or GitHub to fix a bug, and come back to a tested pull request. It runs on your own Claude Code or Codex. Open its work in Orca to review it or step in. [Overview](https://orca.dev/bots) · [Security](https://orca.dev/docs/bots/security) · [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/bots)
### Chat or Terminal Run any agent in Chat UI or as the raw CLI, and move a conversation between the two without losing context. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/agents/native-chat)
### Orchestrate Agents Hand a big task to one agent. It splits the work, starts worker agents in their own workspaces, and brings their results back to you. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/orchestration)
### Run Anywhere Pair a Remote Orca Server, work on any SSH host, or give a worktree its own cloud VM. Your agents keep running when your laptop sleeps. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/ways-to-run)
### Mobile App Pair Orca with the mobile app to get pinged when an agent needs you, reply in chat, and keep work moving on any of your machines when you are away from your desk. [iOS App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) · [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.orca.app) · [Android APK](https://orca.dev/download/android) · [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/mobile)
### Review AI Output Review diffs, leave notes on exact changed lines, and send focused feedback back to an agent. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/annotate-ai-diff)
### Git Integration Draft commit messages and pull requests from the diff, then send failing checks or PR review comments back to an agent to fix. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/commit-push)
### Parallel Worktrees Quickly split tasks into isolated environments, so multiple agents can work side by side without interfering with each other. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/model/worktrees)
### Design Mode Click any element in Orca's browser to copy its HTML, styles, and selector, then paste it into your agent's chat. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/browser/design-mode)
### GitHub & Linear, Native See your GitHub and Linear tasks in one place, and start a workspace for each when you're ready to build. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/linear)
### Orca CLI Anything you can do in Orca, your agents can do too: create worktrees, start workers, drive the browser and desktop apps, and schedule automations, all from the command line. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/overview)
### Plugins Themes, editors, languages, and panels from the community, installed in a click. [Browse plugins →](https://orca.dev/plugins)

**Also in the box:** - **[Bot Schedules & Triggers](https://orca.dev/docs/bots#put-it-on-a-schedule)**: run a bot every weekday at 9, or when a pull request opens, a check fails, or a webhook fires. - **[Bot Memory in Markdown](https://orca.dev/docs/bots/security#what-you-can-review)**: a bot's soul and memory are plain Markdown files (`SOUL.md`, `MEMORY.md`) you can read and edit. - **[Drag Files to Agents](https://orca.dev/docs/editing/file-explorer)**: drag files from the explorer, or images from your desktop, straight into an agent's prompt. - **[Jump Anywhere](https://orca.dev/docs/model/quick-open)**: one shortcut jumps to any workspace or tab across every repo and host. - **[Rich Previews](https://orca.dev/docs/editing/viewers)**: open images, PDFs, and Markdown right in the workspace, next to the agent that made them. - **[Mobile Emulator](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/overview#mobile-emulator)**: run an iOS Simulator or Android emulator beside your agent, and let it tap, type, and check its own work. - **[Dictation](https://orca.dev/docs/settings#voice)**: press a shortcut and talk. Orca types what you say into the agent's prompt or terminal. - **[Usage & Accounts](https://orca.dev/docs/agents/usage-tracking)**: see how much of your agent limits you've used and when they reset, and switch accounts without logging out. - **[Automations](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/automations)**: schedule prompts to run on any repo: nightly dependency bumps, weekly triage, flaky-test sweeps. - **[Computer Use](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/computer-use)**: when there's no CLI or API, agents can see and drive desktop apps and external browsers. - **And many, many more**: we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The [changelog](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases) is the real feature list. --- ## Supported Agents Works with **any CLI agent** — if it runs in a terminal, it runs in Orca.

Claude Code   Codex   Grok   Cursor   GitHub Copilot   Muse   DeepSeek Harness   ZCode   OpenCode   MiMo Code   Amp   OpenClaude   Antigravity   Pi   oh-my-pi   Hermes Agent   Devin   Goose   Auggie   Autohand Code   Charm   Cline   CodeBuddy   Codebuff   Freebuff   Command Code   Continue   Droid   Kilocode   Kimi   Kiro   Mistral Vibe   Qwen Code   Rovo Dev   + any CLI agent

--- ## Install ### Desktop — macOS, Windows, Linux - **[Download from orca.dev](https://orca.dev/download)** - Or grab a build directly: [macOS Apple Silicon](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-macos-arm64.dmg) · [macOS Intel](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-macos-x64.dmg) · [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-windows-setup.exe) · [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-linux.AppImage) · [All builds](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest) _Or via a package manager:_ ```bash # macOS (Homebrew) # Always use the full name; bare `orca` is an unrelated Plotly cask. brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca # Upgrade an existing install brew upgrade --cask stablyai/orca/orca # Release candidates (conflicts with the stable cask; uninstall it first) brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca@rc # Arch Linux (AUR) — or stably-orca-git to build from source yay -S stably-orca-bin ``` ### Mobile App — iOS, Android Pair with your desktop app to monitor and steer your agents from your phone. - **iOS:** [Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) - **Android:** [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.orca.app) · [Download APK](https://orca.dev/download/android) · [Install guide](https://orca.dev/docs/android-apk) --- ## Community & Support - **Discord:** Join the community on **[Discord](https://discord.gg/fzjDKHxv8Q)**. - **Twitter / X:** Follow **[@orca_build](https://x.com/orca_build)** for updates and announcements. - **WeChat:** Scan to join an Orca community WeChat group. - **Feedback & Ideas:** We ship fast. # dsh-our-free-model **简体中文** | [English](README_EN.md)

Trendshift JavaScript 周榜第 1 · 2026-10-05 至 2026-10-11 · 更新中，截至 2026-10-11
> 你只需在 dsh 里装上这个插件，无需登录、注册、填 API Key 或任何其它操作， > 就能用上包括 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Kimi K3 在内的前沿模型——完全免费，不限量。 > > *All you do is install this plugin in dsh: no login, no sign-up, no API key, nothing > else. The frontier models are just there — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and the rest. > Free, with no usage cap.* > > 模型清单跟随上游刷新，可用性由**你自己这台机器的网络出口**实测得出， > 思考强度下发的是真实预算而不是提示词，另附一个 OpenAI 兼容的本地转发端口。 > > 纯插件挂载：不改内核、无构建步骤、零依赖。
--- ## 交流群

QQ 群：974582805（OFM技术交流[2群]）
扫码加入群聊，一起交流插件使用心得、反馈问题与分享玩法。
--- ## 亮点 - **开箱即用，无配置环节**——不需要账号、不需要 Key、不需要在后台申请配额。 - **上游来源公开透明**——免费车道来源为 [OpenCode 的 Zen 网关](https://opencode.ai)，Kilo 渠道来源为 [Kilo AI 的公共网关](https://kilo.ai)，均直连、不经任何第三方中转。请求由谁处理、数据发往何处，见「上游是哪些源」与「免责声明」。 - **清单跟随上游**——模型集合、上下文长度与能力在每次刷新时向上游重新拉取，插件内不保存静态快照。 - **选择器只广播可用的模型**——上游清单已声明但网关明确拒绝路由的模型（返回 `Model is unavailable`、或 404 找不到该 id）从下拉框移除，仅在设置页保留记录并注明拒因；网关自身故障（5xx）、配额限制（429）、超时与断网不属于对模型的判定，一律保持可达；被地区策略拦截的模型归入 region-limited 分组。整轮探测全部被拒时同样保留，选择器不会为空。 - **公告中心 + 实时推送**——仓库维护者在仓库中编辑 JSON 并推送后，所有已安装实例最迟在一个轮询周期内收到；正文为白名单约束下的 HTML，支持图文排版；`urgent` 级别触发全屏弹窗；可选系统级通知。 - **应用内升级**——设置页一键升级：下载 → SHA-256 校验 → 备份 → 原子替换 → 校验回读 → 热重载，任一步失败自动回滚至上一版本。 - **热重载**——升级与代码变更即时生效，无需重启应用；也可在设置页手动触发，或启用文件监视自动重载。 - **按响应体形状判定流式响应**——网关在高负载下会以 `application/json` 的 content-type 返回完整的 SSE 帧序列。插件按响应体形状判定，并将已嗅探的字节重新注入流，既不会导致整轮失败，也不会因 header 与实际内容不符而将可用模型判为不可用。 - **思考强度实际生效**——两类模型两种控制：声明了思考档位的模型（如 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、GLM 5.3 Flash）给出它自己的档位菜单（Off / Low / High / Max 等），选中值按原值下发到上游 `reasoning_effort`，上游会校验该字段、集合外的取值直接 400；没有档位菜单的模型（MiMo V2.6 等）走预算阶梯——Light / Balanced / Deep 对应输出 token 预算 2 048 / 8 192 / 模型上限，思考不可关闭的模型三档整体翻倍为 4 096 / 16 384 / 模型上限，因为思考与正文共享同一输出额度。两者都逐次调用留痕，设置页每张模型卡均标注档位或该档实际下发的上限（详见「思考强度：档位菜单与预算阶梯」）。 - **不依赖浏览器界面**——插件仅将 llm 作为硬依赖，在没有 web server 的 composition（如 dsh-tui）中同样完成启动并输出模型；看板模块挂载在独立的 fiber 上，待 webServer 就绪后再注册路由，因此既不会阻塞模型车道，也不会因插件先于 web 服务加载而永久丢失设置页。 - **用量看板，数据全部留在本机**——Token 热力图、总量曲线（支持总计与单模型视图）、输出速度与首字延迟逐次采样。不上传任何数据。 - **OpenAI 兼容转发端口**——本机其它工具通过 base URL 与 Key 即可调用这些模型。Chat 历史中 assistant 的字符串 `reasoning_content` 会随工具后续请求保留，包括显式空字符串；缺失字段不会被补造。 - **EAC 渠道（桌面端专属）**——在 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端与 DSHEAC AIO 桌面端中自动解锁一条协付通道，模型以 EAC 前缀显示（如 EAC DeepSeek V4.1 Flash）；凭据加密密封，由宿主指纹闸门把守；该渠道在服务器侧校验 GitHub 授权（登录并 star 本仓库）后才放行对话；在命令行及其它宿主中该通道完全不存在。详见「EAC 渠道」。 - **Kilo 渠道（免密免费池）**——内置 Kilo AI 公共网关的免费模型池（`isFree` 清单实时拉取，含 `kilo-auto/free` 自动路由），无需任何账号或 Key；模型卡带 Kilo 徽章。思考强度与 EAC 渠道同款：模型自身的档位菜单（Off / Low / Medium / High，默认 High），经网关统一的 `reasoning` 参数真实下发——Off 已逐家族实测将思考归零（nemotron、ling、dots、poolside、apodex、cohere）；stepfun 与 liquid 端点强制思考（对关闭请求返回 400）、两个自动路由不透传关闭，这些模型的菜单不含 Off 档。该池由上游免费提供，上游会在其模型卡中声明 prompt 可能被记录用于改进服务——请勿发送敏感内容，详见「免责声明」。 - **聚合渠道，自带 Key**——设置页新增一页，把第三方端点接进同一条模型清单：注册表内置 76 家提供商（NVIDIA NIM、OpenRouter、Groq、Cerebras、SambaNova、Gemini、DeepSeek、Mistral、Together、Fireworks、SiliconFlow、Nebius、Chutes、Hugging Face、Cloudflare、Z.ai、Kimi、MiniMax、QwenCloud/Alibaba、Bedrock、Vertex、Vercel AI Gateway、Azure OpenAI、FleetRelay Gateway，以及无需账号的 Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp），写入 Key（本机免账号的提供商不需要）后其模型即以 `provider/model` 出现在选择器里，也可经本地网关调用。Key 只写入本机 0600 的 settings.json，API 只回显 `hasKey` 与 `…abcd` 指纹；每家可单独启停、测试（列表探测，不花一次生成）、发现模型、覆盖 Base URL 与模型清单。OAuth 与 ADC 认证的提供商照常列出，但标注为不可驱动。 - **省 Token**——三件事：工具输出压缩（RTK）在请求发出前就地重写 `tool_result`（git diff / status / log、grep、find、ls、tree、构建日志、编号转储、搜索清单、重复日志行），实测 40 KB 的 `git diff` 移除 90% 的字节且模型仍能就它作答；提示词瘦身有 caveman 与 ponytail 两族、默认全关；另有五个不占用上游请求的本地应答。设置页用与用量图表同一批统计行显示压缩前后字节、节省比例、压缩块数与统计调用数。 - **路由（降级链）**——把任意车道的模型串成一条命名链，以 `combo:` 作为虚拟模型出现在选择器与网关上；`fallback` 固定从链首开始，`round-robin` 轮换起点并连续 N 轮粘滞。链接在输出任何正文之前失败会被整段丢弃，切换对调用方不可见；思考增量不算正文，因此「想了很久才撞上配额墙」正是降级最有价值的场景。 - **本地网关原生说 Anthropic**——新增 `POST /v1/messages`（流式与非流式，含 thinking / tool_use 块、真实 stop_reason 与流内 error 事件）与 `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`（本地估算）；`/v1/models` 广播全部车道，含聚合行与链路。网关页新增「接入客户端」分区，按实际绑定的端口与真实要求的密钥生成 Claude Code、Codex、OpenAI SDK、Anthropic SDK、curl 与局域网的可复制配方。 - **接口具备鉴权围栏**——插件 HTTP 路由优先级高于内核 `/api`，因此内置与内核一致的信任检查（优先复用 composition 的 connection 服务，缺失时退回结构化围栏）。 - **十个账号渠道，一体接入**——LobsterAI（有道）、Qoder / Qoder 中国版（阿里系）、TRAE（字节）、Cline、Loomy（讯飞）、Raccoon（商汤）、MiniMax Code、ZCode（智谱）、Gemini（Google Code Assist）十个账号渠道开箱即用，外加 Kilo 免费车道与原匿名免费通道；OpenCode 账号渠道在本插件中默认停用。各渠道的登录流程、账号池、每日积分领取、模型黑名单与其本地 OpenAI 网关（Chat Completions + Responses，默认 `127.0.0.1:8326`）原样挂载与运行；凭据只写入宿主凭据库，浏览器永远拿不到明文。 - **视觉特效按需开启**——设置页顶部“视觉特效”开关默认关闭，鱼缸和业务功能始终保留；开启后恢复背景光晕、毛玻璃与装饰动画，选择仅保存在当前浏览器。 - **OFM 插件中心：渠道 / 增强 / 页面统一市场**——新仓库 [Ebony-Vinyl/ofm-extensions](https://github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/ofm-extensions) 承载社区插件：Ed25519 签名索引、安装即校验 SHA-256 与静态扫描、运行在 Worker VM 沙箱（唯一 import 是受控的 `ofm:sdk`，网络只放行 manifest 声明的域名，密钥只进不出，每个 hook 带超时熔断）。渠道插件装上即出现在模型选择器（支持 `replaces` 接管内置车道），增强插件以 `onRequest`/`onModels`/`onUsage` 挂进请求链；页面插件在侧边栏贡献一个沙箱 iframe 页面，只能通过受控消息桥读写自己的配置与存储。清单 v1 与 v2 双兼容；内置账号渠道包、聚合渠道目录、客户端启动器、资源库格式与模型工作台也以 built-in 描述符登记在同一插件中心，不可卸载但可查看贡献。发现、安装、更新、启停、配置、密钥、自检、卸载全部在控制台「插件中心」完成；开发者模式可安装本地未签名包（显式风险确认、未验证徽标、同一沙箱）。市场页另带封面横幅、类型色带与骨架屏，详情弹层含签名源码直达链接、发布说明（changelog）与权限清单；索引由宿主后台定时刷新，已装插件的清单可一键导出 / 导入（JSON，不含密钥）用于迁移。模型工作台（magpie）车道的推理请求也接入同一增强钩子链（onRequest），并默认经宿主可替换的 fetch 出站，本机代理类插件（如上下文扩展）重新可见；OFM_ENGINE_PRIVATE_FETCH=1 可回到私有直连。 - **免费车道额度断路器与出口代理（issue #708/#767 的完整回答）**——上游按出口 IP 计免费配额，一次真实 429 即开窗（`Retry-After` 缺省 6 小时），窗口内本插件本地拒绝新回合、不再向墙上送请求；`FreeTierError` 单独锁道。手动测试全部保留（清单刷新/单模型检测/测速），自动探测依旧禁用——状态从真实回合被动学习。车道可配独立出口代理（http/https/socks5），也认 `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` 环境变量；「换出口后重试一次」一键清窗，「测试出口」打第三方回显不花配额。请求形状对齐官方 2.2.3 客户端（`traceparent`/`b3`/通配 `accept`），保留工具名绑定、无对应声明的历史工具调用清理及标题请求免整形；请求适配实现见 `src/o2a/SYNC.md`。 - **十三页毛玻璃界面**——设置页顶部导航扩为十一个页面：原有六页（**免费模型**（鱼缸水位 = 可用模型占比）、**EAC 模型**（鱼缸水位 = 协付池压力）、**白嫖模型接入**（十张渠道卡：登录、账号、模型开关、一键领取积分）、**数据看板**（今日/全部 Token 消耗、平均生成速度、缓存命中率、成功率，账号透视与模型性能表、最近请求总览）、**运行日志**（逐请求明细：结果、耗时、首字、速度、Token 细分，失败原因悬停可见）与**网关设置**（网关开关/端点/密钥；局域网转发中继：监听地址、端口与独立中继密钥）），新增**聚合渠道**（提供商注册表、Key、测试、发现模型、Base URL 与模型清单覆盖）、**省 Token**（压缩开关、两族提示词档位、五个本地应答与节省统计）、**路由**（降级链编辑器）、**插件升级**（版本检查、一键升级与热重载）与**推荐项目**（EAC-Desktop / EAC-Pack / EAC-design-world 三张卡片：简介、直达链接与 Star 按钮，Star / Fork / 最近提交数实时取自 GitHub，取不到就整块不显示）五页；网关设置页另增「接入客户端」分区。页面切换与卡片入场为 150–250 ms 短动效，`prefers-reduced-motion` 下整体关闭。每页都有直达 GitHub 仓库的 Star 按钮。 - **局域网转发中继**——渠道网关本身只监听本机（上游的安全选择）；本插件提供自己的转发门：调用方用插件签发与轮换的中继密钥，转发跳由宿主换用网关凭据（凭据不出宿主进程），仅放行 `/v1/*` 模型接口并带环路保护。 ## 你会看到什么 **输入框的模型选择器** | 分组 | 内容 | | --- | --- | | Our Free Model | 当前网络出口可直接使用的模型 | | `…abcd` 指纹，从不回显 Key 本身；测试与发现模型两次探测也把回包中的 Key 一律脱敏。 转发监听仅绑定回环地址，默认 127.0.0.1，无 Key 请求一律拒绝。将地址改为可路由接口会被直接拒绝（POST /settings 返回 400 并注明原因；在无 web server 的 composition 中手工写入 settings.json 同样不会启动监听）——该端口的流量消耗的是本机这条免密车道，不应由一个字符串决定是否向整个子网开放。 局域网访问是另开的一扇门，并不放宽上述规则：本机监听仍只绑回环、修改地址仍被拒绝；需要跨机器使用时必须显式启用"局域网访问"，中继绑定可路由地址，且每个请求都需携带局域网 Key——连 /、/health 这类存活探针也一并鉴权（仅本机监听免 Key 应答存活探测），否则一个未鉴权的应答等同于向整个子网宣告"该主机正在代理"。中继仅转发 /v1/models、/v1/chat/completions、/v1/responses、/v1/messages、/v1/messages/count_tokens 五条白名单路径（各自的去 /v1 写法同样放行），不代理任意 loopback 服务；入口处将局域网 Key 换为本机 Key，因此两把 Key 互不通用；携带跳数标记的请求直接拒绝（508），因此端口即使配置为本机监听的同一端口也不会自环。局域网 Key 同样由 crypto 生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于同一 0600 文件中，可在面板上单独轮换。 转发 Key 由 crypto 运行时生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于 0600 权限文件中。本仓库不含任何硬编码凭据。/ 与 /health 为存活探针，先于 Key 检查应答，但仅回答"是否在线"，获取模型清单仍需 Key。 插件的 HTTP 路由带请求信任围栏（自 v1.1 修复）：插件的 /api/our-free-model 前缀在 webServer 的最长前缀分发下优先于内核 /api，曾绕过内核鉴权。当前每个请求先经由 composition 的 connection 服务准入（与内核 /api 完全同级的 cookie/token 校验）；connection 缺失的 composition 退回结构化围栏——loopback Host、拒绝跨站 sec-fetch-site、Origin/Referer 必须与 Host 同源同端口，Host 缺失或为空也拒绝（fail closed，不回退至 socket 本地地址）。实测结果：异源 Host/Origin 返回 403，无 cookie 的回环请求返回 401。connection 为逐请求获取，因为浏览器半身要到插件加载之后才将其 provide 出来——若在 apply 时以快照方式读取一次，围栏会在整个进程周期内退化为结构化那一层（本轮将该读取改回快照后，picker-test 的 401 断言立即失败）。 公告 HTML 在客户端经严格白名单渲染：scripts/sanitize-test.mjs 使用 XSS 语料（脚本注入、事件属性、javascript:/data: URL、iframe/svg/form、样式注入、畸形标签）验证全部被丢弃；不经过任何 innerHTML sink。公告源的 feedUrl 可被用户指向任意 URL，因此渲染器按不可信输入处理。 应用内升级的完整性链（v1.3.2 加签）：清单 Ed25519 签名验证（公钥 pin 在 src/updater.js，无签名或验签失败的清单直接拒绝，未签名镜像不会被安装）→ 清单校验（semver、路径逃逸、哈希格式、base 必须为清单相对路径）→ 下载时逐文件校验 SHA-256 与字节数 → staging 回读校验 → 安装后回读校验 → 任一步失败即恢复备份；安装前强制重新拉取清单，杜绝陈旧清单。文件与代码边界见已知边界一节。 更新通道与 feedUrl 彻底解耦（v1.3.2）：feedUrl 仅重定向公告 feed，永不再重定向升级清单——此前一个设置项即可将升级源指向任意服务器并配以自配平的哈希，等同于将"修改一个设置值"升级为"在宿主进程中执行任意代码"。公告 override 本身也收紧为仅 https（回环 http 除外，本机镜像与测试仍可用）且不得内嵌凭据。目标域不受限制：任何 https 地址均可作为 feedUrl，插件按 feedPollMinutes 的间隔轮询——因此在不含 connection 服务的 composition 中（见上文鉴权说明），能够修改设置的本机调用者可让进程持续请求任意外部地址。这与插件的其余外联一样按"设置即信任"对待：能够修改 settings.json 的人本来就能安装代码。 转发监听仅绑回环地址，且按解析结果绑定（v1.3.2）：localhost 这类主机名先经 dns.lookup 解析、全部结果均为回环才放行，绑定使用解析出的 IP——当 hosts 文件或企业 DNS 将 localhost 指向可路由接口时，校验与监听不再各自为政。 卸载只需移除 bundle 条目，插件不留任何补丁；其数据目录为纯 JSON，可直接删除。 ## 许可证 本仓库自己的代码是 MIT，见 LICENSE。第三方组件和数据的许可证见下一节「致谢」。 本项目为独立插件，与任何模型提供方无隶属、认可或赞助关系。使用该插件访问免费额度受各提供方 自身条款约束；在超出个人机器的场景中部署前，请先确认这些条款。 ## 致谢 感谢 Jet（iJetLi）的渠道包（`vendor/channel-pack/`，MIT；上游仓库 [dsh-providers-hub](https://github.com/iJetLi/dsh-providers-hub)）—— 十个内置账号渠道的登录、账号池与本地网关都出自这里，许可证与出处见该目录下的 LICENSE 与 NOTICE.md。 也感谢这些项目： - [models.dev](https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev)（MIT）：模型窗口、输出上限与思考档位。目录数据按 MIT 使用，许可证全文见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。 - [9router](https://github.com/decolua/9router)（MIT）：`scripts/probes/` 下 8 个取证脚本的原始来源——那 8 个文件是逐字副本（只改了探测的 base URL），文件头保留了 MIT 归属，许可证全文见 [LICENSE](LICENSE#9router--mit)。它们 import 9router 自己的模块，只在该项目的 checkout 内可运行，不进发行集。 - [magpie-muse-web](https://github.com/JohnWangggg/magpie-muse-web)（上游未声明 SPDX 许可证）：`muse-web` 桥接扩展的上游。 **以下项目在本仓库里不再有任何代码或数据**，只作为历史记录保留： - [opencode2api](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api)（GPL-3.0）：免费车道请求整形的最早参考。2.8.6 已把相关实现重写并删除其资产，当前代码与该项目的文件没有共享文本、函数名或常量表；现在只按 [sst/opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode) v2.2.3（MIT）生成的官方资产工作，见 [维护说明](src/o2a/SYNC.md)。 - [free-claude-code](https://github.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code)（AGPL-3.0-only）：供应商目录与五个本地应答的最早参考。2.8.6 重写本地应答、按 models.dev 重建目录；只剩五个优化 id 与部分 provider id 作为**持久化配置键**沿用（改名会让用户已关掉的开关静默复活），见 [兼容说明](docs/provider-compatibility.md)。 - [trae-mate](https://github.com/luckymiaow/trae-mate)（MIT）：TRAE 签到流程的早期参考，已被重写取代。 - [dsh-cline-pass](https://github.com/codeOct/dsh-cline-pass)（MIT）：Cline 额度与请求记录的早期参考，已被重写取代。 - [rtk](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk)（CLI Apache-2.0，engine BUSL-1.1）：工具输出过滤器的最早参考。`src/token-saver/compact/` 已全部重写，仅保留 RTK 的输出标记与阈值——那些标记是模型读惯的线格式，改掉会改变模型行为而不是让代码更原创。2.8.6 的替换范围见 [验证记录](docs/verification/2026-11-18-independent-core.md)。 根目录的 MIT 只覆盖 OFM 自己写的代码；上面仍在使用的组件和数据按各自许可证提供，完整条款以上游 LICENSE 为准。这份名单是来源记录，不改变任何组件的许可证。 ## Star 趋势 图表由 Star History 自动更新，无需手动提交图片。受服务缓存（当前为 24 小时）和 GitHub 图片缓存影响，显示可能延迟，并非秒级实时；点击图表可查看在线趋势。

items.description: dsh-go — DeepSeek Harness 装进口袋：手机本机运行，也能遥控你的电脑。
items.readme_text:
简体中文 · English

DeepSeek Harness 的手机应用：Android 版已发布；iOS 版仍在开发和真机测试，需在 Mac 上自行签名编译（iOS 工程 · 架构）。


Trendshift 全语言日榜 #1 · 2026-10-30


Deepy 和鲸娘，陪你干活

干活时敲代码，做完来个空翻，等你确认会举手。打开「App 外显示」，它们还会跟你到桌面。


下载 DSH Go

从 GitHub Releases 或官网下载页获取最新版 APK，常见手机选 arm64 包。

 

感谢大家对 DSH Go 的支持和喜爱！当前下载页提供 Android APK；iOS 版还在开发和真机测试，没有公开安装包，鸿蒙版也在继续推进。

第一次用可以先看使用指南，遇到问题欢迎来论坛和 QQ 群。
手机上装过签名不同的早期测试包时不能直接覆盖安装，需要先卸载旧版；卸载会清空对话、Linux 环境和设置。


本机运行，也能遥控电脑

内置 Linux 环境，免 Root、免 Termux。电脑上的 DSH，也能一键切过去接着用。


插话、打断，过程自动收好

回复中途也能插话，排队的消息随时「立即发送」。做完的过程折叠成一行。


原生界面，也有网页版

和官方网页版一键切换，停在同一段对话，下次打开还是你上次用的那个。


分享卡、对话回放和链接

回复一键做成分享卡。整段对话生成链接，对方在浏览器里回放，链接端到端加密。


横屏与平板

横屏手机和平板重新排版：侧栏常驻，内容居中，弹出键盘也不挤。


主题配色与桌面图标

六套主题色，也能跟随壁纸或自选颜色。四款桌面图标，三种功能图标风格。


中文，也说 English

全部界面支持英文，在设置里切换，默认跟随系统。


手机操控

看屏幕、帮你点，三档确认随你选。敏感操作默认交还给你；放宽应用规则或解除限制前，请先了解风险。


## 可以做什么 DSH Go 提供聊天界面、本机运行环境和远程连接，是基于 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的第三方项目。运行在手机上的是 DSH 引擎；模型请求仍由你配置的模型提供方处理。 - **本机运行**：在 App 内安装 Ubuntu、Node.js 与 DSH 运行环境，无需 Root 或另装 Termux。 - **远程连接**：通过 SSH 或李国宝老师开发的 [DSHarness Remote](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote) 使用电脑、服务器上的 DSH。 - **聊天与工具**：切换模型，发送图片、使用语音输入，处理工具审批和提问；支持聊天界面与网页模式。 - **插件界面**：使用适配 DSH Go 的原生工具卡、表单和面板；仓库提供 SDK、教程和示例。 - **手机操控**：在你开启权限后，让本机引擎读取屏幕、点按和输入，并可随时停止。 - **分享与外观**：分享、导出和回放对话，调整主题、图标和桌宠。 功能随主机和连接方式不同。DSHarness Remote 当前只支持图片附件，不能在 App 内打开网页版，插件管理限于开关，且不支持 DS Bot 和对话日志导出。详见[本机引擎与远程主机](docs/guide/zh/03-engine-hosts.md)。 ## 安装 安装要求为 Android 8.0（API 26）及以上。Release 页面上的 **arm64** 安装包适用于常见的 64 位 Android 手机；x86_64 设备和模拟器用的 x64 包在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。仓库没有 32 位 ARM 构建。 1. 从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/releases/latest) 或[官网下载页](https://go.dshtui.com/download)下载对应架构的 APK，并按系统提示允许该安装来源。 2. 首次启动时，选择在本机安装运行环境，或连接远程主机。 3. 为所选主机配置模型和所需凭据，再开始对话；部分远程渠道需要在主机侧配置。 仅连接远程主机时，不必在手机上安装本机运行环境。手机操控只对正常模式下的本机引擎开放，需要按界面说明开启无障碍等权限；不打扰模式另外要求 Android 14 及以上，以及 Shizuku 或自连 ADB。首次使用可按[使用指南](docs/guide/README.md)逐项配置。 本地引擎默认使用 PRoot 兼容启动。开发者选项中的直接启动默认关闭，开启后的兼容性和回退方式见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。当前 Android 构建以 APK 侧载为目标，不是 Google Play 发布配置。 ## 数据与权限 模型请求会发送给你配置的提供方。开启手机操控后，任务需要的屏幕文字可能发送给模型，支持看图的模型也可能收到截图；请先阅读 App 的权限说明。 “发送匿名使用统计”默认开启，可在首次引导或“设置 → 隐私与分享”关闭。采集范围和关闭后的处理见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。分享内容前，请检查预览；收到链接或文件的人可以保存其中的内容。 ## 风险提示与免责声明 DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方项目，与 DeepSeek 无关联，也不代表 DeepSeek。使用前请了解： - **AI 并非万无一失**：回答、代码和操作可能出错，也可能被网页、消息或文件中的恶意指令误导。请核验重要结果；医疗、法律、投资等高风险决策不应仅依赖 AI 输出。 - **工具会产生真实影响**：本机或远程主机上的命令、文件修改及手机操控可能导致数据丢失、隐私泄露、账号、资金或设备损失。免确认、放宽应用规则或解除限制会减少保护；确认与拦截机制不能保证消除所有风险。建议保留默认保护，只授予必要权限，不在存有支付或银行信息的设备上解除限制。详见[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。 - **第三方服务与费用**：模型、远程主机和插件等按各自条款运行；相关数据处理、服务可用性和费用取决于你选择的服务与配置。本机运行不等于模型离线，也不代表数据不会离开设备。 - **使用前做好防护**：备份重要数据，只连接可信主机、安装可信插件，留意模型用量与费用；不要让 AI 无人值守地处理不可逆或高风险任务。 - **无担保与责任范围**：在适用法律允许的范围内，本软件按“现状”提供，不保证准确性、持续可用性或满足特定用途；相关无担保及责任限制见 [LICENSE](LICENSE) 第 15–17 条。本声明不排除或限制依法不得排除或限制的责任，也不减损你依法享有的权利。 ## 常见问题
和 DeepSeek 官方是什么关系？
没有关系。DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方客户端，基于开源的 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 构建。手机上运行的是 DSH 本身；模型请求发给你配置的模型提供方，需要联网，按你在提供方的账户计费。
安全吗？
本机网页版只接受 App 自己的访问。分享链接端到端加密，密钥只在链接里，服务器看不到内容，但获得完整链接的人可以读取并保存内容。手机操控默认保留敏感操作保护；放宽应用规则或开启「解除限制」会减少这些保护。安全机制不能保证零风险，详见[风险提示与免责声明](#风险提示与免责声明)和[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。
切到后台会被杀吗？
部分系统的省电策略会拦住后台。DSH Go 发现后会提醒你，并直达对应的放行设置，vivo、小米、华为、荣耀、OPPO 都有。
对手机有什么要求？

items.description: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow: profile Python, Node or Ruby apps, port the hot functions with your coding agent, prove they behave the same.
items.readme_text:
Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow.

Rewriting a whole app in Rust costs months, minute-long compiles and gigabytes of `target/`. Most of the runtime sits in a few functions anyway. **fast-anything** finds those functions, has your coding agent port *only them* to Rust, proves the port gives the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. One command, fully reversible.

## Install ```sh npm i -g @el4cteo/fast-anything # or: cargo install fast-anything ``` Ports are compiled with your Rust toolchain ([rustup](https://rustup.rs)). ## Use ```sh fast-anything go --agent claude -- python app.py # or: -- node app.ts / bun app.ts / deno run -A app.ts / ruby app.rb / java App.java / mvn exec:java / gradle run / go run . / php app.php / clang -O2 main.c / Rscript app.R ``` Or step by step: | command | what it does | |---|---| | `scan -- ` | profiles the app, ranks functions by time × how portable they are | | `port [id]` | records up to 500 real calls, creates a one-function Rust crate + `TASK.md` | | `verify` | release-builds the port and replays every recorded call | | `enable` / `disable` | swaps the Rust in or out (one marked block, removed byte for byte) | | `bench` | times the whole app, original vs Rust, interleaved runs | | `report` | markdown + SVG card for your PR | | `doctor` | checks Rust, your runtimes and your agents | `--agent` takes `claude`, `codex`, or any command that reads a prompt on stdin. Without it, hand `TASK.md` to whatever you use. ## Proof, not vibes

That port looked right but compared bytes instead of characters. 148 of 500 real calls caught it. On top of the recorded calls, fast-anything derives extra cases and lets the original answer them: edge cases (NaN, ±infinity, -0.0, zero and ±1, non-ASCII text, empty and up to 16× bigger inputs) and shrunk inputs (tiny and random slices). Nothing is enabled until every case matches: same values (floats within 1e-9), errors where the original errors. A port that is right but slower per call than the original (calling into Rust costs more than the work saved) isn't enabled either. `FAST_ANYTHING_DISABLE=1` runs the original any time. ## Results Real runs on an i5-10500, Windows 11 (C and C++: a 4-core GitHub Actions Linux runner). Reproduce them from [`examples/`](examples). | app | before | after | |---|---|---| | Python fuzzy dedupe (700 names) | 4.91s | **42ms, 116×** | | TypeScript fuzzy dedupe (2,000 names) | 3.11s | **155ms, 20×** | | PHP fuzzy dedupe (600 names) | 2.94s | **53ms, 55×** | | Go fuzzy dedupe (3,000 names) | 3.02s | **144ms, 21×** | | Ruby fuzzy dedupe (400 names) | 3.13s | **228ms, 14×** | | C# fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 4.03s | **312ms, 13×** | | Java fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 3.50s | **1.18s, 3×** (11× on the function; the rest is JVM startup) | | C mandelbrot (8 zoom levels) | 431ms | **127ms, 3.4×** | | C++ fuzzy dedupe (6,000 names) | 3.02s | **1.09s, 2.7×** | fast-anything ports the outermost loop it can, not the tiny function called inside it, so the app crosses into Rust once instead of millions of times. Porting only the inner `levenshtein` gave 35× and 1.9×. ## Why not rewrite it all? - **Compile time**: each port is a one-function crate. Seconds, not minutes. - **Cache**: every port shares one `.fast/target`. Delete it whenever you like. - **Risk**: your code stays as it is. Rust is opt-in per function, checked against real behavior. ## Agents - **Claude Code plugin**: `/plugin marketplace add EL4CTEO/fast-anything`, then `/plugin install fast-anything@fast-anything` and `/fast-anything:fast python app.py` - **MCP server** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…), built into the binary: `claude mcp add fast-anything -- fast-anything mcp`. 8 tools: `fast_scan`, `fast_port`, `fast_verify`, `fast_enable`, `fast_disable`, `fast_bench`, `fast_report`, `fast_status`. - **Skill**: [`skills/fast-anything`](skills/fast-anything/SKILL.md) teaches any agent the loop. ## Languages | language | binding | status | |---|---|---| | Python 3.10+ | PyO3 | ✅ | | JavaScript / TypeScript (Node 22+, Bun, Deno 2+: `bun app.ts`, `deno run -A app.ts`) | napi-rs | ✅ | | Ruby 3.3+ | C ABI + JSON, through Ruby's built-in Fiddle | ✅ | | Java 22+ (`java App.java`, Maven, Gradle) | the same C bridge, through the FFM API | ✅ | | Kotlin/JVM (Gradle, `src/main/kotlin`, JDK 22+) | the Java bridge; top-level functions, `object` and companion members, extension functions | ✅ | | Go 1.22+ (`go run .`) | the same C bridge, through the Windows loader or dlopen (cgo) | ✅ | | PHP 8.1+ (`php app.php`) | the same C bridge, through PHP's FFI extension (`extension=ffi`) | ✅ | | C and C++ (gcc, clang or Intel oneAPI icx/icpx: `clang -O2 main.c lib.c`) | the same C bridge, through LoadLibrary or dlopen | ✅ | | C# / .NET 8+ (`dotnet run -c Release`) | the same C bridge, through NativeLibrary; profiled with EventPipe, nothing to install | ✅ | | R 4.0+ (`Rscript app.R`) | the same C bridge, through base R's `.C()`; profiled with Rprof, no packages or R headers needed | ✅ | It ports top-level, deterministic functions that take plain data (numbers, strings, lists, dicts, typed arrays…), including ones in your entry script when its main code sits under `if __name__ == "__main__":` (or `if __FILE__ == $0`, or `if (import.meta.main)` / `if (require.main === module)`). In Python that means module-level functions and `@staticmethod`s (dataclasses, NamedTuples and numeric NumPy arrays count as plain data), in Java, C# and PHP static methods (and PHP functions), in Go plain functions, in C and C++ free functions and static methods. `scan` says why anything else can't move yet. With Intel oneAPI on Windows, run fast-anything from a shell where `setvars.bat` ran (it sets up the linker). SYCL kernels run on the device and aren't ported; with `-fsycl`, only host functions are profiled and ported. Ruby, Java, Go, PHP, C, C++, C# and R need no headers, bindings or extra tools: the port is a plain Rust library with one C entry point taking and returning JSON, and fast-anything replays the recorded calls against it directly. Any language that can call C can use that bridge. ## License MIT

Understand how it works, down to the binary level.** [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/morluto/rea?style=flat-square&logo=github)](https://github.com/morluto/rea/stargazers) [![Monthly npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/rea-agents?style=flat-square&label=npm%20downloads)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rea-agents) [![MIT license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-f4c430?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Join the REA Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-5865F2?style=flat-square&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/GkcryMnJDM) [![Follow REA on X](https://img.shields.io/badge/X-000000?style=flat-square&logo=x&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/reatools) [![Supported platforms: macOS, Windows, and Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS%20%7C%20Windows%20%7C%20Linux-4493F8?style=flat-square)](docs/getting-started/installation.md) [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/morluto/rea?style=flat-square)](https://skills.sh/morluto/rea/reverse-engineer-anything) **[Website](https://rea.tools/) · [Guides](https://rea.tools/guides/) · [Showcases](https://rea.tools/showcase/)** [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Showcases](#showcases) · [How REA works](#how-rea-works) · [What you can analyze](#what-you-can-analyze) · [Build RL environments](#build-rl-environments) · [FAQ](#faq) · [Documentation](#documentation) npx rea-agents setup
> [!IMPORTANT] > Get REA from [morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea), > [rea.tools](https://rea.tools/), or the [rea-agents npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rea-agents). > Follow the installation and release links from these official sources. A similar > repository name or copied README does not establish that a download is official.




Join the Reverse Engineering Community
Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell

--- See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine. ## Quick start **[Get started at rea.tools](https://rea.tools/get-started/)** for step-by-step instructions by operating system, agent, and analysis provider. ### Connect your agent (MCP) With [Node.js and npm](docs/reference/supported-targets.md) installed, run this from a trusted directory outside the project you plan to analyze. ```bash npx rea-agents setup ``` Choose your agent, review and approve the setup plan, then restart your agent. Setup backs up existing configuration and adds REA's MCP connection and investigation skill. See the [installation guide](docs/getting-started/installation.md) for supported clients, plugins, manual registration, and troubleshooting. Try asking your agent: ```text Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. ``` Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand. ### Use REA from the terminal (CLI) Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR: ```bash npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json ``` The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows. To install the `rea` command for regular use: ```bash npm install --global rea-agents rea --help ``` For native analysis, configure a provider first. The [CLI and Evidence guide](docs/getting-started/cli.md) covers provider selection, native commands, snapshots, and scripting. For Linux prerequisites, see the [installation guide](docs/getting-started/installation.md#linux-owned-process-prerequisite). ### Update REA For a global npm or Bun installation, run the updater and follow its setup instructions. ```bash rea update ``` If you use `npx`, refresh your agent setup with: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` Review the setup changes and restart your agent. See [update and uninstall instructions](docs/getting-started/installation.md#diagnose-update-and-remove) for package runner options and troubleshooting. ## Showcases

DX-Ball: reconstruct a sound-pan calculation

Recover a position-to-pan helper from x86 instructions and verify the C reconstruction against 3,205 original-x86 cases and all 63 compiled function bytes.

Read the case study · Reconstruction repository

Notion: trace the Electron clipboard bridge

Follow the renderer’s clipboard API through preload and IPC into the main process to see how Notion handles rich clipboard data.

Read the case study

TH04: recover a DOS bullet-ring calculation

Recover fixed and aimed angle calculations from the PC-98 game’s 16-bit instructions and compare the reconstructed C++ with historical compiler output.

Read the case study · Reconstruction repository
If you've used REA on something interesting, we'd love to see it. Share your case in an [issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) or a [pull request](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls), including the target, your question, how REA helped, and what you found. ## How REA works Your agent uses REA through MCP to inspect a target and trace the relevant code. It can use the evidence REA returns to ask follow-up questions, explain behavior, or build and test an implementation. The CLI uses the same workflows. ![REA investigation flow: your agent asks about a local target, REA inspects and traces it using analysis tools, and the agent uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test.](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg) [Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg). ## What you can analyze REA covers native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, websites, .NET assemblies, Android apps, firmware, and recorded runtime and network activity. [Supported targets and requirements](docs/reference/supported-targets.md) For native decompilation, choose a provider that supports your target format and host OS. See [choosing a deep analysis provider](docs/reference/supported-targets.md#choosing-a-deep-analysis-provider). ## Build RL environments Build a local environment from a recorded web session or a Linux desktop app so an agent can practice a task and check its result. [Build an RL environment with REA](https://rea.tools/guides/rl-environments/). ## FAQ
Which agents can use REA? Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the [supported agents](docs/getting-started/installation.md#supported-agents); other clients can use [manual MCP registration](docs/getting-started/installation.md#mcp-registry).
Do I need a native analysis engine? Deep native analysis uses Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna, depending on the target and operation. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native analysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval; Ghidra, IDA and Kuna use your existing installations. See [provider setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md#hopper) for the options and their supported targets.
Do I need to start Hopper first? REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may ask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the same user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open Hopper manually if needed. See [Hopper startup and troubleshooting](docs/getting-started/installation.md#launcher-paths-and-troubleshooting).
What does installing the skill from skills.sh do? The skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent. Use `npx rea-agents setup` to register REA's MCP server and install the matching instructions, then restart your agent. See [skill-only installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md#skill-only-installation).
What code does REA return? Native analysis returns pseudocode and assembly. JavaScript/Electron analysis recovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to write and test an implementation; the [showcases](#showcases) give worked examples.
Does REA upload my app? REA analyzes targets locally. Your agent receives the tool results, and its model provider has its own data policy.
What should I do if I hit a bug? Update first; a recent release may already fix it. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` For agent setup through `npx`: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` If you're using an agent, complete the [setup refresh](#update-rea) and restart it. Retry the same task. If the problem persists, [open an issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) with your REA version, target type, steps to reproduce and error output.
## Documentation Start with the website's [worked guides](https://rea.tools/guides/). Craft Anything

English · 日本語 · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Tiếng Việt · Português · ไทย · Türkçe

See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust.
Point it at a target, say what you want, and it studies the original with real inspection tools,
has a coding agent build a new project, checks the result against the original and refines it.


Download Craft Anything · ArtCraft · All Crafting Apps



A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers, > filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil > last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

How it works · Two ways to use it · AI · Agents · Under the hood · Get started · Status · Downloads · Discord


🔍 Study anything

Websites, desktop apps, phone apps, games and files: real inspection tools find out how they're built and what they do, with the evidence behind every answer.

🛠️ Build your own

Say what you want ("Recreate this website", "Recreate this game's gameplay in Rust") and a coding agent builds a new project in the stack you ask for.

✅ Checked, not guessed

Every build is compared with the original (pages at three screen widths, a game's own self-test, an app's runs) and refined until it's close.

🤖 Agent-ready

320 tools, each one a CLI command and an MCP tool, so any agent can drive the same engine the app uses. No AI is needed to inspect.

## How it works Point Craft Anything at a target, say what you want, and press Start. It works in four steps, asking you in plain words when a decision is yours: 1. **Study:** inspect the original: its pages at every width, its code, its files, how it runs. 2. **Build:** a coding agent builds a new project, in the language, framework or engine your request names (or a sensible default). 3. **Check:** compare the build with the original and list what doesn't match yet. 4. **Ready:** open, play or preview the result, or ask for changes and it refines it.

Make: pick what to recreate, say what you want, press Start.
Ready: play the game, or ask for changes below.
## Two ways to use it - **Simple** (default): "What do you want to make?" Pick a website, app or game, describe it, press Start. A project page shows the four steps (Study → Build → Check → Ready), what the agent is doing in plain words, question and approval cards, how alike the result is, and buttons to open the result or its folder. Ask for changes in the box at the bottom. "Just look inside" opens a target for questions without building anything (in Deep mode). - **Advanced**: the full workbench: every tool (Ctrl/Cmd+K), functions, strings, pseudo-C, disassembly, hex, call graphs, evidence, unknowns, jobs, logs and the agent console. Both modes drive the same engine. ## Clean room or Deep - **Clean room** (the default): nothing inside the original is read, not its code, files or page source. Craft Anything works from what you can see: pictures you add, the website as a visitor sees it (screenshots, visible text, measured layout, colours, fonts and spacing, menus opened) and, when you allow it, a picture of the app's window. Tools that would look inside are refused and say how to turn on Deep mode. - **Deep**: every tool is used, for your private use. A program's code and files are read with the built-in engines (and Ghidra when it's installed), a website's JavaScript is read and its start page watched, and the builder may use all of them. Clean room is a rule about what Craft Anything offers and refuses. It is not an operating-system sandbox: it doesn't isolate your computer. A coding agent you run still acts as you, and what it can read, write or run depends on its own permissions. Which of an agent's own tools Craft Anything can refuse differs by agent; for Claude Code's tools in chats and questions, see [`docs/claude-code.md`](docs/claude-code.md). Switch in the title bar or Settings, with `settings_set deep_mode true`, or for one CLI run with `--deep` (or `--clean-room`).


Advanced: functions, pseudo-C, the agent and the evidence behind every answer.

## AI Building needs a coding agent on your computer. **Claude Code** is supported first: Craft Anything runs your own, unmodified `claude` program, which uses your own sign-in; Craft Anything never sees or handles your account. Your use of it falls under your own agreement with Anthropic. See [docs/claude-code.md](docs/claude-code.md) for how and why. A Codex adapter exists but hasn't been verified on a real install yet. **GitHub Copilot** can use your installed Copilot CLI through ACP: sign in separately with `copilot login`. **Grok Build** can use your installed `grok` program through ACP (`grok agent stdio`): sign in separately with `grok login`. See [docs/grok.md](docs/grok.md). Other agents that speak ACP (Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, opencode, goose, Hermes, Maki, Devin) can be switched to it per backend; of those, Maki and Devin have been run live (Devin authenticates with the backend's stored key — its own CLI sign-in doesn't count over ACP). Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, xAI (Grok, when `XAI_API_KEY` is set) and local OpenAI-compatible servers are available for questions and analysis (Settings → AI). ## Built for agents Every tool is also a CLI subcommand and an MCP tool, so an agent can study a target or run a whole rebuild without the app: ```sh craft-anything-cli commands # every tool, by toolset craft-anything-cli mcp # serve them to any MCP client craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website" ``` Results are evidence records with their confidence, coverage and limitations; big ones come back as a summary first and are paged with `core_evidence_browse`. `craft-anything-cli setup` connects Craft Anything to coding-agent apps. ## Under the hood A pure-Rust reverse-engineering engine with 320 tools (300 in the engine, the rest from the AI and setup layers) for native programs, .NET, Java, Android, Apple, Electron/JavaScript, websites, firmware, packet captures, databases and game files. Its own decoders, disassembler and decompiler work without any outside program; Deep mode uses them all, and Ghidra when it's installed. It powers the desktop app (egui), the CLI and the MCP server, and parts of it run in the browser as WebAssembly. The full list is in [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md). ## Get started Requires Rust **1.97 or newer** (a dependency needs it; `rustup update`). On Debian or Ubuntu, the desktop app also needs: ```sh sudo apt-get install build-essential libxkbcommon-dev libxkbcommon-x11-0 libwayland-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libgtk-3-dev ``` Then: ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything && cd craft-anything cargo run --release -p craft-anything # the desktop app cargo install --path apps/craft-anything-cli # the CLI, as `craft-anything-cli` craft-anything-cli doctor # checks the install, coding agents and engines ``` Building needs a coding agent signed in on your computer (see [AI](#ai)); `doctor` says what's missing. Rebuild from the command line (questions are asked in the terminal): ```sh craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website" craft-anything-cli rebuild - "A snake game in Rust" --rounds 1 craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Make the header blue" --continue-in "" craft-anything-cli rebuild - "Add a contact form" --project-folder "" --existing edit ``` New projects go in `Documents/Craft Anything` (change it in Settings → General). Each project folder holds `craft.json` (the request, target, status and history), `capture/` (what was recorded from the target), `app/` (the generated project), `checks/` (each comparison against the original), `investigation.cany/` (evidence) and `inbox/` (open questions). A project can also start in a folder you pick (Choose a folder… under Start, or `--project-folder`). If it already has files, you say what they are: the app itself, which the builder edits in place, or material to start from, with the app built in `app/` beside them (Settings → General can remember the answer). Settings → General also lists projects from more folders; removing one only takes it off the list. ## Status > [!IMPORTANT] > **Status:** Craft Anything is in early alpha. What works today, what is partial and what's next: > > - **Works today:** the desktop app (Simple and Advanced), the CLI and the MCP server; the > Study → Build → Check → Ready workflow for websites, apps and games with Claude Code as the > builder; website checks at three screen widths; game rebuilds in Unity, Unreal or Godot; Deep > mode with Ghidra; generated pictures and 3D models (opt-in, your own fal.ai key); plugins (MCP > servers, and WASM components in builds with the `wasm-plugins` option). > - **Partly there:** building with API keys and other coding agents (built, not yet run live), > behaviour checks for apps and games, a few engine tools tested only against stand-ins. > - **Released:** public releases with installers for Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD are > published on the [Releases page](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases); they are > still alpha. > - **Next:** the managed tier. > > [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) has the detail and how each part was checked, > [docs/tool-status.md](docs/tool-status.md) the tool-by-tool checklist, and > [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) the plan, item by item. Please file issues, or tell us what > broke on [Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft). **Responsible use.** Use Craft Anything on software you own or are allowed to examine. It never bypasses DRM, logins or anti-cheat. Rebuilds recreate layout, style and behaviour from evidence; the agent is told not to copy logos, photos or text unless you confirm you own them or have permission. **Installing dependencies runs code.** When a builder installs a project's dependencies, the commands run on your computer, and the packages can run code while they install. npm runs each package's install scripts by default, and Rust build scripts and Python source packages run their own setup code. Craft Anything asks before a command of a kind it hasn't seen in this project (`npm`, `cargo`…). Choosing "always allow" for `npm` lets every later npm command run without asking, so only do that for a project whose dependencies you trust. To install npm packages without their install scripts, run `npm install --ignore-scripts`. ## Downloads On GitHub, the [latest release](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/latest) has every build listed below, and [all releases](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases) has earlier versions and their notes. `` in the file names is the version number, and `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists a checksum for every file. ### Windows | Build | Installer | Portable | |---|---|---| | x64 (64-bit Intel/AMD) | `craft-anything--windows-x64.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-x64-portable.zip` | | arm64 (Snapdragon and other ARM PCs) | `craft-anything--windows-arm64.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-arm64-portable.zip` | | x86 (32-bit) | `craft-anything--windows-x86.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-x86-portable.zip` | Installers and executables are code-signed. The portable zip keeps its settings next to the app. ### macOS | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | App, universal (Apple silicon + Intel) | `craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg` | Signed and notarized | | Command-line tool, universal | `craft-anything-cli--macos-universal.zip` | Signed and notarized; see below if macOS blocks it | Versions after 0.2.0 include the command-line tool in the app, so builds don't need the separate zip. You only need it to use the command line without the app. A browser download of the zip can stop with "Apple could not verify craft-anything-cli" (a lone program can't carry its notarization with it, so macOS has to look it up online). A download from the terminal isn't checked this way, so use this instead: ```sh ver=0.2.0 # change this to the version you want curl -fLO "https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/download/v$ver/craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal.zip" ditto -x -k "craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal.zip" . mkdir -p ~/.local/bin mv "craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal/craft-anything-cli" ~/.local/bin/ ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli --version ``` To run it as just `craft-anything-cli`, add `~/.local/bin` to your `PATH`. If you already have the blocked copy, press Done (not Move to Bin), then run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine `, or allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. #### Checking that a Mac download is signed and notarized Each Mac release is signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. To check a download yourself, run these in Terminal (replace `` with the version and the paths with yours): ```sh # The disk image: "accepted" and "source=Notarized Developer ID" mean it passed spctl --assess --type open --context context:primary-signature -v "craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg" # The notarization ticket is attached: prints "The validate action worked!" xcrun stapler validate "craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg" # The app, after you open the disk image: the signature must verify codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "/Volumes//Craft Anything.app" spctl --assess --type execute --verbose "/Volumes//Craft Anything.app" # The command-line tool: a bare program can't carry a ticket, so macOS checks it online codesign --verify --strict --verbose=2 ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli codesign -dv --verbose=4 ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli 2>&1 | grep Authority ``` The `Authority` lines should name a "Developer ID Application" certificate. If a check fails, don't run the file; report it with the output and the release tag. ### Linux | Format | x86_64 | aarch64 (ARM64) | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | AppImage | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.AppImage` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.AppImage` | Runs anywhere; updates itself with [AppImageUpdate](https://github.com/AppImageCommunity/AppImageUpdate) (`.zsync` files) | | Flatpak | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.flatpak` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.flatpak` | Sandboxed, so it can't start a browser on your computer, which studying websites needs (use another package for that); `flatpak install --user ` | | Debian/Ubuntu | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.deb` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.deb` | | | Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.rpm` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.rpm` | | | Tarball | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Unpack anywhere | RISC-V (riscv64): `craft-anything--linux-riscv64.tar.gz`, a tarball only. The AppImage carries the CLI too: run ` --cli ` (for example ` --cli mcp` for an MCP client), or make a link to the AppImage named `craft-anything-cli` and run that. ### FreeBSD | Build | File | |---|---| | x86_64 | `craft-anything--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | ### Web (WebAssembly) | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | Browser viewer | `craft-anything-web-.zip` | Says what a file is, in the browser (the file never leaves it); host the folder on any static web server ([packaging/web/README.md](packaging/web/README.md)) |

Come make things with us

Our Discord is where artists of every kind hang out: people who paint, shoot, draw, cut film, set type, and people still figuring out what they like to make.
